name: docs-layered-libraries
body:
Layered-libraries how-to (docs/layered-libraries.md): a repo `docs/layered-libraries.md` is the how-to for a two-layer library. It works through a two-layer example — a deck whose `kalide.yaml` sets `templates: ../shared-lib` and which also holds a deck-root `templates/` directory — and states the cross-layer rules: the layers merge with no precedence; a name (slide or section, theme, or shared `media/` path) carried by both is an error naming the name and both paths; a reference in a template or theme resolves in its own layer while a local template's `section` helper call resolves across the merged namespace; the external layer is self-contained and validates standalone; a `{{ template }}` layout-composition call names a layout by its root-qualified layout path and a local layer may include an external-layer layout while an external-layer layout naming a local-layer layout is a templates error (guide-layout-composition, example-layout-composition); and changing the configured `templates:` value while serving requires a restart (template-retarget-requires-restart). README.md links to it.

AC: docs/layered-libraries.md exists and is linked from README.md; it carries a two-layer example and states the merge and uniqueness rules, own-layer references, the cross-layer `section` call, external standalone validation, layout composition across layers, and retarget-needs-restart.
